_meta.description: Human-curated, frozen link-safety allowlist for outbound links the site (and, longer-term, an automated link-vetting step) treats as trusted: the reputable-outlet table from CLAUDE.md's corroboration procedure, every content/companies/*.json official_domains[] entry, every citation/source_url hostname actually used in content/frontier_board.json and content/companies/*.json as of the Phase 6 stage-3 build, and arXiv's API/site hosts. This is deliberately separate from schemas/company.schema.json's own official_domains[]/official_repos[] fields (which are PRIMARY-source-classification inputs for the analyst's corroboration procedure only, per that schema's own description) -- this file is the outbound-link-vetting allowlist, a different concern with a different owner.
_meta.curation: This file is human-curated and frozen. It must never be regenerated automatically, rewritten wholesale, or edited by the automated daily analyst/verifier Routine or any other automated pipeline step -- additions/removals are a deliberate, logged decision at an owner/PM checkpoint, the same discipline CLAUDE.md's reputable-outlet table itself is held to.
_meta.path_scoped_note: 2026-07-21 curation pass closed the gap this note used to describe: content/companies/moonshot-ai.json and zhipu-ai.json now populate official_repos[] (https://huggingface.co/moonshotai, https://huggingface.co/zai-org), and path_scoped[] now carries the two matching entries (huggingface.co/moonshotai/*, huggingface.co/blog/zai-org/*) covering exactly the two huggingface.co citations already live in frontier_board.json/content/companies/*.json (moonshot-ai's Kimi-K2.6 model card, zhipu-ai's GLM-5.2 blog post) -- both live-verified as real, on-topic, non-redirecting pages before this change, not trusted blind. Still never add a bare github.com/huggingface.co to hostnames -- both remain multi-tenant hosts; any future huggingface.co/github.com citation outside these two prefixes needs its own path-scoped entry, the same way. cursor.com was added as a bare hostnames[] entry in the same pass (not path-scoped) since it's a single-tenant corporate blog, not a multi-tenant host -- live-verified (xai.json's cited Grok 4.5 post) before adding.
_meta.2026-07-25_addition_note: An end-to-end fact-check pass across all 13 tracked companies added 13 new frontier_board.json rows, each independently fetched and verified (not trusted from a first-pass research summary) before its citation was written. Three new single-tenant hostnames added here as a result, each live-verified as the real, on-topic, non-redirecting page actually cited: docs.mistral.ai (Mistral Medium 3.5's model-card overview), nvidianews.nvidia.com and blogs.nvidia.com (NVIDIA's own newsroom/blog properties, citing the Nemotron 3 Nano and Super/Nano Omni announcements respectively).
_meta.2026-07-26_addition_note: The first live end-to-end run of the daily analyst/verifier/profiler Routine drafted a card citing https://claude.com/blog/the-new-rules-of-context-engineering-for-claude-5-generation-models -- Anthropic's own blog, live-verified (fetched successfully by both the analyst and, independently, the verifier) but on a hostname (claude.com) distinct from the already-trusted anthropic.com/platform.claude.com. The pipeline correctly refused to add it to this file itself (frozen-file guard) and instead blocked the run and escalated to the owner. Owner explicitly authorized trusting claude.com the same day; added here as its own standalone commit, never bundled with the commit that uses it. The same run also cited https://www.debian.org/vote/2026/vote_002 (Debian's own official vote page) for a second card -- the owner was also asked about that one and explicitly declined to trust debian.org. www.debian.org is deliberately NOT in this file as a result, and the card that depended solely on it was dropped rather than published without a trusted citation; a future Debian-sourced story would need to raise this again rather than assume the earlier claude.com approval extends to it.
_meta.2026-07-27_addition_note: The second daily Routine run drafted three cards citing hostnames not yet in this file, each live-verified as the real, on-topic, non-redirecting page actually cited before this decision, not trusted blind: blog.cloudflare.com (Cloudflare's own blog, its new per-category AI-bot-traffic-controls post), siepr.stanford.edu (Stanford's own SIEPR policy-brief page on AI and jobs), and github.com/slvDev/esp32-ai (an independent developer's own project repo for a microcontroller-scale LLM). The pipeline again correctly blocked the run and escalated rather than adding any of these itself. Owner approved trusting all three the same day. blog.cloudflare.com and siepr.stanford.edu are added as bare hostnames[] entries -- each a single-tenant official site, the same discipline docs.mistral.ai/nvidianews.nvidia.com were added under on 2026-07-25. github.com is deliberately NOT added as a bare hostname -- per this file's own path_scoped_note above, it remains a multi-tenant host -- instead path_scoped[] gains one narrow {github.com, /slvDev/} entry covering exactly this citation and no other github.com content; any future github.com citation outside that prefix needs its own path-scoped entry, the same way moonshotai/zai-org's huggingface.co entries already work.
